A real miner change now fails on identity and must be re-seeded in a reviewed diff, which is the intended cost. It also makes edgeEvidenceSeparation nullable on the committed side (a perfect miner reports no false edges, and requiring a number here made the goal state un-seedable) and hardens the reproduction walk to own, plain-object keys (Object.create(realReport) had no own keys, serialized as {}, and reproduced). schemaVersion 9 answers an eleventh round that showed schemaVersion 8 pinned the wrong half of the report: ledgerDigest covered the row-level ledgers, so a producer-side change could still DELETE meanCausalEdgeStrength or meanCausalEdgeZ, or forge causalCouplingsLostToCap, meanFalsePairConfidence or confidenceSeparation, and return a clean PASS — the summary layer where the advertised measurements live was pinned by nothing but re-derivation inside the process that produced it. reportDigest replaces it and covers EVERY field, containers included (an array emits its length and an object its sorted key list before their contents, so a deleted field is not merely fewer records). Number quantization moved from 4 decimals to 9: at 4 a uniform strength-0.00001 applied across the whole producer reproduced the digest exactly, and 9 still sits five orders of magnitude above the libm last-bit noise that made rounding necessary in the first place. The reproduction walk now reads each field ONCE from its own property descriptor (Reflect.ownKeys, data descriptors only, enumerable only): an enumerable getter had been returning the real value to the comparator and a different value to the next consumer, and an extra non-enumerable own property was invisible to Object.keys and to JSON.stringify but not to a plain read. A baseline seeded from a perfect run (null separation, zero false edges) now forces falseEdgeGrowth to 0 rather than inheriting the tolerance, which is what the separation-exemption comment had always claimed. The cost of pinning the whole report is that an IMPROVEMENT also fails, on identity — `npm run bench:correlation -- --seed` prints the block to commit, and that re-seed diff is where a human reads the new numbers. schemaVersion 10 answers a twelfth round that found two things reportDigest could not see, because the report never carried them. Rule probes reported two booleans and a sentence about a fixture the report did not contain: re-aiming a near-miss at a clause the rule still has — moving n1b off GDACS while deleting the earthquake-tsunami distance check — left the positive matching, the near-miss rejecting on the source gate instead of the radius, and every leaf of the report identical. Each probe now carries a fixtureDigest over both fixtures' full event fields and the expected outcomes, so what was ASKED is pinned alongside the answer. And the pair ledger erased the two things the engine actually asserts about a pair before hashing: rewriting a rule from causal-candidate cause->effect to contradicts effect->cause was byte-identical in the report, while production maps both the edge type and the endpoint order into the evidence graph. Emissions are now rows of their own — ruleId, edgeType, and directed fromId/toId — and the unordered key stays the grading key, because planted truth is a claim about two events being related, not about which came first. This file also gained a witnessed block: the advertised-but-ungated measurements (meanCausalEdgeStrength, meanCausalEdgeZ, meanFalsePairConfidence, confidenceSeparation, causalCouplingsLostToCap) plus one digest per ledger, pinned by value. reportDigest already covered all of it; what it did not do is SHOW it, so the re-seed diff the digest prescribes reading was a single opaque 32-character string. No graded number moved in this re-seed — every metric above is identical to schemaVersion 9's. schemaVersion 11 answers a thirteenth round that found the twelfth round applied each of its fixes to only HALF of the surface it named. The pair ledger kept direction and edge type, but the LEARNED-pair ledger still counted: `emissions: number`, so rewriting every learned rule from causal-candidate to contradicts — the opposite assertion, and a different evidence edge downstream — left all 101 rows and the report digest byte-identical. Learned-pair rows now carry the same BenchPairEmission[] the built-in ledger does, and every emission in a row must name that row's rule and hash to that row's key. Rule probes pinned what was ASKED but not what was ANSWERED: five of the nine shipped rules never fire over the golden corpus, so the probe is their only observation, and inverting airquality-wildfire from causal-candidate to contradicts preserved both booleans, the fixture digest and the report digest. Probes now record positiveEdgeType and positiveDirection — the emitted edge type and the emission-order endpoints — and the gate range-checks both. And a probe still tested ONE clause: the earthquake-tsunami near-miss held the GDACS source gate valid while varying only distance, so deleting the source clause left the rule accepting any nearby humanitarian event with the probe still reporting a clean rejection. Near-misses are now PATCHES on the positive fixture, one per independently-defeatable clause — 59 clauses across 9 rules, up from 9 — and a copy cannot drift from the positive except in the field it names. Two clauses per rule is the enforced floor, duplicate clause labels are refused, and the domain-gate near-misses move BOTH events: `domainMatches()` in correlate-engine.ts is a DISJUNCTION over the pair, so moving one event out of a rule's domains does not reject it. Finally, the witnessed block compared causalCouplingsLostToCap through a comma join, which is not injective: the single element "macro->maritime,space->infra" joined to the same string as the real two-element array and passed. List comparison goes through JSON, which keeps element boundaries.
